name: threshold-slider
title: Threshold slider
description: Set warning and critical levels on one track: two handles divide it into OK, Warning and Critical zones, named in words and shown by pattern.
docs: value is { warn, critical }: the warning starts at warn and the critical zone at critical, with OK below. min, max and step set the scale, unit is written after the numbers (a symbol such as % sticks to the number, a word such as ms stands apart) and zoneLabels renames OK, Warning and Critical. The handles never cross and never come closer than minGap (one step by default). Each is a slider with a 44px target and a spoken value that says the zone it opens ("Warning starts at 70 percent"; spokenUnit changes the word for the unit). The zones are told apart by tone, pattern and name: plain, hatched and dotted, so they read in monochrome and for colour-blind people. A scale under the bar shows the ends and both levels in tabular figures, and a number that would touch its neighbour makes way. The legend names and measures each zone ("OK to 70%, Warning 70 to 90%, Critical above 90%"), and each handle has its own number field, clamped between the other handle and the limits. Arrow keys move one step, Shift or the Page keys ten, Home and End go to the limits, and a press on the bar moves the nearest handle. onValueCommit fires once when a drag or a key press settles.
